note: One entry per CONFIRMED fix. Audit leads that are not confirmed do not belong here. States are NOT stored here: the runner writes them per build identity to the results folder.

entries.title: Model import must not overflow the stack on deeply nested JSON
entries.originalFailure: A 200 KB GLB whose extras nest 100000 levels crashed the importer (exit 0xC00000FD, stack overflow); the JSON parser accepts deep nesting, the recursive URI check did not.
entries.testStrength: Mixed: the nested-URI refusals and the ordinary-model validation are real assertions; the 300000-level case can only fail by crashing the suite (a crash leaves later checks NOT-CHECKED).

entries.title: Plain-cube posed bounds are exact and build/cache no geometry
entries.originalFailure: bounds_at built and cached a new mesh for every changing plain-cube box (tumbling debris), causing about 125000 geometry-cache misses, 370 MB of never-reused meshes and long waits on the cache's exclusive lock in rock-break scenes.
entries.testStrength: Strong for equivalence (500 random poses bit-identical to the mesh walk) and for no geometry built. The performance effect is measured separately (stress runs) and is not asserted by this check.
investigate: HANDOFF-KEYCARD-20261004.md section RESULT: EXACT PLAIN-CUBE BOUNDS

entries.title: Real fracture fragments never fall back to a bounding box
entries.originalFailure: One 1921-point shell shard of a baked statue could not be built as a hull and was replaced by a counted bounding box.
entries.testStrength: Strong for the tested statue; says nothing about other geometry. No runtime speed benefit was demonstrated; do not treat this as a performance fix.

entries.title: A reduced collision hull is never accepted beyond the deviation bound
entries.subsystem: physics hull builder (deep/Physics/PhysicsWorld.cpp BuildHull first-reduction path)
entries.originalFailure: The first reduced hull (more than 256 vertices needed) was returned whatever its error and only counted as over bound.
entries.testStrength: WEAK: dense spheres measure 0.46% against the 0.5% bound, so no input available reached the changed branch. The checks guard the bound property but did not fail on the old code. An injected-bound or adversarial input is still needed.

entries.title: The physics C ABI refuses hostile input instead of passing it to Jolt
entries.originalFailure: Non-finite or zero-quaternion poses, non-positive density, oversized index counts, null arrays, non-finite velocity or platform moves, and removal of a stale body id reached Jolt unchecked.
entries.testStrength: Strong for the refusals it names: with the old code the suite fails at the first EL-07 check, and with the fix all 19 pass and valid calls still succeed. Does not cover EL-07 items it does not list (slp_add_hull poses are covered through AddShape; terrain heights length cannot be checked because the ABI has no length parameter).
investigate: deep/Physics/PhysicsWorld.cpp CheckPose, Add, slp_body_velocity, slp_character_remove, slp_character_platform, slp_character_actor

entries.title: A rope that fails part-way leaves no half-built links
entries.originalFailure: AddCable pushed the cable before its links and constraints existed, so a later failure such as body capacity left unconstrained links in the world and the cable list, ticked every step.
entries.testStrength: Strong for body-capacity failure: with the old code the suite fails at the last EL-08 check (slots not given back); with the fix all four pass. Covers only the capacity failure path, not other throws inside the build.

entries.title: A failed terrain tile cook is reported and recooked instead of ending the process or leaving the tile not ready
entries.originalFailure: A terrain tile cook that throws on its std::async worker ends the process, because the physics module is compiled with _HAS_EXCEPTIONS=0 (Jolt's setting); the audit expected a permanently not-ready tile. A cook failure was never reported or retried.
entries.testStrength: Strong for an injected cook failure on all 36 tiles: they are reported as errors, a later terrain update recooks them and the terrain becomes ready. With the hook but without the guard the process terminated at the first failure (0xC0000409). Real Jolt mesh failures have not been produced; failure is injected through slp_debug_fail_cooks.

entries.title: Failed D3D12 map, reset, close and signal results on the startup and per-frame paths are reported instead of being ignored
entries.originalFailure: Map, command allocator Reset, command list Reset and Close and the per-frame fence Signal results were discarded; after a failure the frame kept recording into a closed or unreset list, wrote through null mapped pointers, or waited on a fence that was never signalled.
entries.testStrength: Strong for the sites that now go through the checked call: each reachable checked result is failed in turn (27 on the reference machine) and must surface as a create or frame error or a cleanup error, with a fresh viewport working afterwards. The hook exists only on the fixed sites, so it cannot show that no other unchecked D3D12 call remains; the unbounded fence wait is unchanged and device-loss behaviour with a real removed device is not tested.
investigate: deep/engine/render_device.h remaining unchecked D3D12 calls and waitFence INFINITE

entries.title: A device failure during viewport destruction is recorded and cannot terminate the process
entries.originalFailure: sl_destroy let flush(), drainRetired or teardown throw out of a noexcept unique_ptr deleter, ending the process instead of reporting the session error.
entries.testStrength: Moderate: a failed fence signal during the destruction flush is injected and must be recorded as a Viewport cleanup error without terminating the process. Only the flush step is injected; failures in the other guarded steps are covered by the guard code but not by a test.

entries.title: The scene-preparation stage always joins its worker, and completion is separate from progress
entries.originalFailure: An exception from the message pump, loading screen or observer destroyed a joinable std::thread and ended the process; and the loop stopped pumping as soon as the work first reported full progress, leaving the window unserved while post-work ran.
entries.testStrength: Strong for the runner itself: with the old exit rule the keeps-being-served check fails (verified by mutation). The throwing-display case is tested through the runner, not through a full prepare_scene with a real loading screen. Cooperative cancellation of the worker is not added; the post-work duration in a real scene is not measured.
investigate: editor/cpp/adventure.hpp early fraction=1.0 at the end of prepare_geometry

entries.title: A scene that names one object id twice is refused
entries.originalFailure: Duplicate Character ids passed validation although caches, runtime maps and commands key by id; only command-time lookup rejected them.
entries.testStrength: Moderate: validate, encode and decode all refuse a repeated id and the full suite still accepts every scene it builds; the 4 shipped scenes have no duplicates. The count, route-length and identifier-length caps from the same audit item are NOT done: they need agreed limits that keep all authored scenes valid.
investigate: editor/cpp/scene.cpp object count, Route length and Id length limits

entries.title: Each object's geometry is pinned before it is warmed so eviction cannot remove it in between
entries.subsystem: object cache and scene preparation (editor/cpp/adventure.hpp prepare_geometry, object_cache.hpp)
entries.originalFailure: Preparation warmed an object's geometry and pinned it afterwards; another preparation thread's insert could evict it in between, so it was rebuilt during play (a late build).
entries.testStrength: Strong: under a one-byte budget the old order rebuilt 105 of 112 objects, the current order none (verified by reverting the order). Covers the geometry pin race on the real preparation threads; the bounds-entry pin and tree-memory budget are not separately exercised.
investigate: editor/cpp/object_cache.hpp bounds pins under instance eviction

entries.title: A file read that fails part-way is reported instead of returned as a complete (truncated) file
entries.originalFailure: read_file built its string through an istreambuf_iterator, which ends quietly when the underlying read fails; a locked byte range or lost volume returned a truncated prefix that atomic_write's expected-hash check, the file watcher, hashing and loading treated as the whole file.
entries.testStrength: Strong for the reproduced failure: a locked byte range makes the old read_file return a prefix and the new one throw (verified by running the old code, which fails the truncated-read check). Files up to 1 MB read back identically. Not covered: a disconnected volume, files growing while read, hash_file streaming (not changed here), and the ED-10 hash bookkeeping.
investigate: hash_file still loads the whole file

entries.title: A failed physics update does not leave its time in the fixed-step accumulator
entries.originalFailure: A Jolt update error was thrown before the tick was subtracted from the accumulator, so the failed time stayed and the next call replayed it; a lasting capacity failure made the backlog grow on every call.
entries.testStrength: Strong for the error path: with an injected update failure the next step advances exactly one tick identical to a control world; with the reset removed that check fails (verified). The real Jolt capacity error was not produced. NOT covered: the accumulator limit for ordinary slow frames (owner decision) and the CharacterStep double advance (EL-13).
investigate: deep/Physics/PhysicsWorld.cpp accumulator growth when frames stay slower than 200 ms

entries.title: The editor's disk-hash bookkeeping after a save no longer depends on re-reading the file
entries.originalFailure: After saving, the editor re-read the file to compute its hash; a failed re-read (lock, antivirus) left the hash stale so the next save failed with a false 'File changed; reopen before saving'.
entries.testStrength: Moderate: save_scene returns the exact hash, and a whole-file lock shows the old re-read fails; the editor wiring is a one-line use of the returned hash and is not exercised by a test. The load side (hash of a second read after open) is NOT fixed.
investigate: editor/cpp/editor_main.cpp Open and startup --scene hash_file calls
load_scene returning the hash of the bytes it decoded

entries.title: The asset browser scan can be cancelled so closing the editor does not wait for it
entries.originalFailure: A std::future from std::async waits for its task in its destructor, so an asset-folder scan on a slow share held up closing the editor for as long as the scan ran.
entries.testStrength: Moderate: the scan honours a cancel flag (already-set flag stops it at once, unset flag changes nothing). The editor's destructor wiring and the shutdown delay on a real slow share are NOT tested, and a single blocking filesystem call cannot be interrupted. The preset-check task (presetTask) is not changed.
investigate: editor/cpp/editor_main.cpp presetTask and projects.cpp child process wait
real shutdown delay on a slow network folder

entries.title: A Characters entry that is not an object is refused with the intended message (one sub-item of the audit item)
entries.originalFailure: from_json called j.value() before checking the entry was an object, so a non-object raised a JSON type error instead of 'Expected Character object'.
entries.testStrength: Weak-to-moderate: asserts the exact message for four non-object forms, but the old behaviour was not run for comparison. The other CC-23 sub-items (tutorial progress reset, STARLIGHT_ASSET_LIBRARY length, stoi in the graphics runtime, CoInitializeEx) are NOT done.

entries.title: A zero lightning seed gives the default bolt instead of a degenerate straight line (one sub-item)
entries.originalFailure: Zero is a fixed point of the xorshift generator, so every bolt generated with seed 0 was the same straight unjittered line.
entries.testStrength: Weak-to-moderate: seed 0 now equals the default bolt and other seeds still differ; the old behaviour was not run for comparison. Other EL-21 sub-items are NOT done.
investigate: sl_lightning computing the mesh twice for a size query
